claims.statement: Use Barony's six home resources to fund early choices, but do not treat the old round-one double-tech suggestion as current default advice.
claims.conditions: The source describes Arc Prime and Rentera as a four-resource and two-resource home; Barony has two commodities and competing spending needs.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463, July 2026, discussing Thunder's Edge; guide-era advice, not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers explicitly contrast an older double-tech line with their newer reluctance; the home resource values come from their read of the faction sheet.

claims.statement: Prioritize Graveliche Maneuvers over a single ordinary technology when the choice is real; accept a slower follow-up round or a discarded secret if needed.
claims.conditions: Especially valuable in the opening, where its movement affects multiple ships and systems; first consider available card routes, scoring, and secret-objective cost.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's Thunder's Edge discussion; not a universal priority for older rulesets.
claims.uncertainty: The recommendation is emphatic, but how to finance it varies by strategy-card order and available objectives.

claims.statement: Treat Diplomacy, Trade, and Imperial as distinct ways to pay for or support the breakthrough, with different timing and opportunity costs.
claims.conditions: Diplomacy can refresh after spending; Trade supplies money; Imperial's secondary can finance it if available, while Leadership may provide a token and secret redraw line.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's Thunder's Edge opening discussion; card order and table choices govern availability.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers disagree on card ranking, and throwing away a secret or yielding Imperial to another player has real costs.

claims.statement: Draft a slice with meaningful influence and preserve command-token access; the home resource pool does not fix either shortage.
claims.conditions: The speakers suggest about six influence in the slice as a minimum and accept lower slice resources more readily than lower influence.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463; slice composition and token pressure are table- and map-dependent.
claims.uncertainty: Six influence is a rough guide threshold, not a tested minimum or universal rule.

claims.statement: Politics supports a plausible round-two Mecatol Rex and Custodians attempt, but Barony must assess Titans and other competing fleets.
claims.conditions: Best when movement, order, and fleet strength allow Barony to follow an initial approach or contest the center; deal-making may matter.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463, Thunder's Edge setting; no point is guaranteed.
claims.uncertainty: The Titans comparison is a qualitative matchup judgment, not a resolved combat result.

claims.statement: Trade and Politics are consistently high picks; Leadership, Diplomacy, Tech, Construction, and Warfare depend on slice, scoring, and opening tempo.
claims.conditions: Construction can substitute for Warfare's reach when Graveliche is active; Warfare rises for useful secondaries or an objective, and routine double-tech is discouraged.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463; strategy-card rankings are explicitly disputed between speakers.
claims.uncertainty: One speaker favors Construction over Warfare in some contexts; the other rates Warfare lower. Preserve both views.

claims.statement: Graveliche lets non-fighter ships move at the highest movement value among ships that began together in the system; use a fast escort to tug slower ships.
claims.conditions: Ships must start in the same system and move together; Gravity Drive or temporary movement bonuses may raise the shared movement value.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463 discussion of the Thunder's Edge breakthrough; Fighter II as a tugboat is described only as an unusual edge case.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers note that interpretation had a ruling and might be revisited; this summary does not establish present-day legality.

claims.statement: Do not reflexively delay Graveliche to buy Gravity Drive: the guide says its broad movement can matter more than one ship's extra movement, while Gravity Drive remains useful.
claims.conditions: Applies when choosing the round-one breakthrough versus technology; reassess if a specific early destination requires extra reach.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's Thunder's Edge advice; source mentions a ruling-era interpretation that may change.
claims.uncertainty: This is a sequencing recommendation and explicitly not a claim to abandon Gravity Drive.

claims.statement: If nearby, the Scepter of Emelpar can refund resources spent on Graveliche and leave Barony resources for technology or ships.
claims.conditions: Relic must be available, reachable, and worth taking; speakers prioritize its resource refresh over the influence as the reason for this line.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463; relic discussion is conditional on the map and Thunder's Edge content.
claims.uncertainty: The guide offers this as a high-priority opportunity, not a guaranteed opening.

claims.statement: Destroyer II is a high-impact early option for Fracture and Mecatol contests, fighter pressure, and deterrence.
claims.conditions: A small fleet with Destroyer II, a carrier, fighters, and infantry can challenge a lightly defended Fracture system; inspect the actual board and ground force.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463, Thunder's Edge setting; specific Fracture-system examples are map-dependent.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers differ on how early to buy it; one ranks it above Gravity Drive, while the other says prior games sometimes had spare movement.

claims.statement: A recurring core package is Gravity Drive, Non-Euclidean Shielding, and Carrier II; Destroyer II is a strong competing early priority.
claims.conditions: Use as a flexible tech priority shaped by objectives, skips, timing, and access to X-89; Non-Euclidean Shielding improves each sustain by cancelling two hits.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's Thunder's Edge discussion; technology advice is not a current-rules verification.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers agree on the package's value but differ on the relative priority of Destroyer II and Gravity Drive.

claims.statement: The guide de-emphasizes Dreadnought II and accepts Direct Hit risk, while favoring Destroyer II more than earlier Barony advice did.
claims.conditions: This advice is framed around the new movement/fleet toolkit and the flagship's strong ability; account for the value of an actual Direct Hit risk in the game.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463 contrasts past base-game concerns with the newer Thunder's Edge context.
claims.uncertainty: This is a changed strategy opinion; one speaker prefers Destroyer II and the first speaker had not previously prioritized it.

claims.statement: Use Graveliche's combat modifier on a meaningful roll, but do not over-optimize small probability differences; the agent can add a die to a chosen ship.
claims.conditions: One proposed heuristic targets the most dice when not using Munitions Reserves, or a low hit chance when rerolls are available; then use the agent on the ship with the best resulting hit chance.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463; combat-modifier interpretation and die arithmetic are reported advice, not separately verified.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers explicitly disagree about how much the fine-grained optimization matters; emphasize the useful-combat heuristic over a single exact formula.

claims.statement: Munitions Reserves spends two trade goods at the start of each space-combat round to reroll any number of Barony's ordinary combat dice once for that round.
claims.conditions: Does not reroll Space Cannon, Bombardment, or Anti-Fighter Barrage; a later combat round has a new use window.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's explanation of the faction ability; no current-rules review.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers clarify its window through a confused exchange; the final explanation says it may be used each round, not repeatedly within one round.

claims.statement: Armada raises Barony's non-fighter ship cap by two above its fleet-pool token count, allowing two ships in a system at zero fleet tokens.
claims.conditions: Taking fleet tokens for tactics may be more practical than for other factions; the speakers also note Barony may still field five ships when another rule sets a general cap of four.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463; agenda and objective interactions are described as occasional edge cases.
claims.uncertainty: The guide's proposed exceptions to fleet-token-loss effects and fleet-size objectives are conditional and not independently rules-checked.

claims.statement: Do not chase a zero fleet pool for its edge-case benefits: Armada protects a minimum ship count, but Barony still needs tokens to activate systems and avoid being stalled.
claims.conditions: The no-token interactions apply only to effects that specifically remove a fleet-pool token; they do not remove other token or action costs.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463 combines Armada discussion with slice/token-economy caveats.
claims.uncertainty: The episode's edge-case agenda interpretations are informal and not rules-verified.

claims.statement: Keep a Dunlane Reaper mech in reinforcements if you want the deploy option; each use replaces an infantry at the start of a ground-combat round for two resources.
claims.conditions: There must be an infantry to replace and a mech in reinforcements; only one deployment occurs in that round, so resources alone do not deploy several mechs.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463 component explanation; deploy is described in the speakers' rules terminology.
claims.uncertainty: The guide presents keeping one in reserve as a flexible option, not a mandatory build plan.

claims.statement: Field Arc Secundus when its shield removal and self-repair can swing a space combat, accepting that Direct Hit remains a risk.
claims.conditions: At the start of each space-combat round opposing units lose planetary shield and the flagship repairs; its strong ability rewards use when combat matters.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's flagship discussion; ability and unit stats are not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: One speaker recommends using it despite Direct Hit risk, while also describing the cost as a constraint on their own games.

claims.statement: Sell or trade War Funding for value, planning around its post-roll timing and the fact that Barony cannot initiate a trade while defending.
claims.conditions: The holder can reroll all opponent dice and any number of their own after a space-combat roll; a defensive buyer must already hold it.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463 describes the Omega note in use; exact text and rules status have not been independently reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Because it rerolls misses as well as hits, the result can worsen; speakers differ on whether to wait for the window or accept any offer.

claims.statement: Plan for a cash-poor faction despite the resource-rich home; Trade, midgame Leadership, and negotiated deals can address recurring spending needs.
claims.conditions: Barony spends on rerolls, mechs, tokens, and ships; which income line works depends on card access and table willingness to trade.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's Thunder's Edge discussion.
claims.uncertainty: The podcast describes economy qualitatively, not from a measured sample; unusual commander income is treated separately.

claims.statement: Barony can use credible force projection to bargain or extort when a reachable opponent is ahead or exposed.
claims.conditions: Needs movement, enough ships and tokens, and a target with something worth trading; the guide's example is a late-round threat backed by fleets that could converge.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463 strategic anecdote and opinion, not a general negotiation rule.
claims.uncertainty: The specific round-four example succeeded in one described game; success and table reaction are uncertain.

claims.statement: After Rear Admiral Farran unlocks, each Barony unit that uses Sustain Damage can yield one trade good, but ordinary income is modest and Pillage can intercept it.
claims.conditions: Commander unlock requires five non-fighter ships in a system; very large sustain-and-repair loops require other players' components/resources and a combat that can eventually end.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463; speakers debate an unusual infinite-money-style edge case and do not resolve all rules questions.
claims.uncertainty: The eight-to-ten trade goods estimate is a rough personal estimate; no infinite-income claim is endorsed.

claims.statement: Negotiate for other factions' sustain and repair interactions when they benefit both players; Nomad's Cavalry can make a Barony ship especially durable under Non-Euclidean Shielding.
claims.conditions: Depends on alliance/promissory access, resources to repair, and a combat that can end; Empyrean, Titans, and Nekro examples range from ordinary to highly unusual.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's proposed table deals; not guaranteed or current-rules verified.
claims.uncertainty: The extended loop examples are speculative and have a debated stopping condition; the guide's ordinary Cavalry deal is firmer advice.

claims.statement: Balance space control with infantry needs; Barony can run short on infantry, and the speakers suggest trading for Sol's Military Support as extra help on the ground.
claims.conditions: Infantry also supplies replacements for Dunlane Reaper deployments; without X-89 access, the speakers sometimes prefer defending space over assuming a ground win.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463; alliance and X-89 availability depend on the table.
claims.uncertainty: The ASR renders the note as ‘souls mill support’; the reference file names Military Support. The recurring infantry shortage is one speaker's experience.

claims.statement: Seek mutually useful technology or combat deals with Jol-Nar and Last Bastion; access can improve Destroyer II/X-89 plans or add Galvanize dice to Barony's combat toolkit.
claims.conditions: Trade support, fragments, or other value only when tempo and expected scoring justify the cost; Galvanize can interact with Graveliche, the agent, Munitions Reserves, and Destroyer II.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463; no access is guaranteed and Support for the Throne retains its normal scoring cost.
claims.uncertainty: Examples are negotiated possibilities and include the speakers' personal trade preferences.

claims.statement: Aim for an early center and Fracture schedule—Mecatol Rex around round two and Styx around round three—using Graveliche and reinforcements to beat opponents to the ground-tech contest.
claims.conditions: Requires enough ships, tokens, and movement; use forward docks or separate fleets to stage follow-up forces and assess who can arrive first.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463's Thunder's Edge plan; round and destination are strategic targets, not promised outcomes.
claims.uncertainty: The guide warns X-89 can reverse a ground contest and says round-three Styx is harder without Non-Euclidean Shielding or substantial plastic.

claims.statement: Treat Crimson as a severe matchup warning when its flagship can suppress Barony's sustain edge in the contested system; the speakers offer no reliable answer in that position.
claims.conditions: The concern is strongest at Mecatol Rex or Styx when Crimson's flagship and associated ability are present and protected.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463 matchup opinion, with Thunder's Edge-era component references.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers state that they do not know a dependable counter; this is not a claim Barony always loses to Crimson.

claims.statement: Consider Malice or a valuable equidistant when it can address Barony's influence and money shortages or stage a later leverage play.
claims.conditions: The planet must be available and strategically affordable; its central staging value matters if Barony plans later force projection.
claims.compatibility: Episode 463 map advice; local objectives, competition, and diplomacy govern the choice.
claims.uncertainty: The guide says competition for Malice is lower than before, but does not establish availability or safety in a particular game.

connections.conditions: Gravity Drive or another movement boost raises the fast escort's value, allowing Graveliche to carry slower ships that began with it.
Non-Euclidean Shielding improves the value of the flagship's sustain when it is exposed to hits; the flagship also repairs itself at the start of each combat round.
When a unit sustains damage, commander income may be generated; repeated sustain-and-repair ideas depend on enough resources and a combat that can end.
If Cavalry grants a Barony unit Sustain Damage, Non-Euclidean Shielding increases its hit-cancellation value; negotiate a price that both players accept.
In a combat where Barony fields the Destroyer II fleet, choose the agent's extra die for the ship with the best post-Graveliche hit chance.
If reachable and available, its resource refresh can reimburse early breakthrough spending, preserving resources for a later build or research.
The matchup is especially difficult if Crimson's flagship can suppress the sustain plan at the contested Mecatol Rex or Styx system.
Pillage can intercept the commander's one-trade-good-at-a-time income when Mentak is able and willing to trigger it.
Trading for Sol's Military Support can help Barony replenish infantry for ground defense and Dunlane Reaper replacements.
